title: The coat and the uncle
venue: the coast community-college paper, Newport · the laundromat digest
source: lore/drift_wood/_THE_COMPLETE_RUN.md (1999–2000 · deepening xix · the daily filled)
logline: Monday. The uncle looks at the coat. Says it's a good coat. Wood says it's a thrift-store coat. The uncle says that's what he said. The uncle's own coat, on the chair's back, is the same coat thirty years older. Nobody says that either.

panels.composition: The shack. The UNCLE in the chair, the oxygen line. WOOD in the chore coat. GULLY at the tank. BARNABY.

image.prompt: an old man in a lawn chair with an oxygen line looking at a young man in a canvas chore coat inside a bait shack, a teenager at a tank, a dog, black and white, no words

panels.composition: The uncle's own coat on the chair's back: canvas, thirty years, the cuff gone entirely, a button that doesn't match.

image.prompt: close on an old canvas work coat hung over a lawn chair's back with its cuff worn away and a mismatched button, black and white, no words
image.notes: The uncle's coat: the same coat, thirty years on. Unremarked.

image.prompt: a young man looking at an old coat on a chair and saying nothing, black and white, no words

panels.composition: The shack. Two coats. One on a man, one on a chair. The strip draws them the same and lets the reader do the thirty years. Six strokes.

image.prompt: a bait shack interior with a young man in a canvas coat and an old coat draped on a lawn chair, drawn in six sparse strokes, black and white, no words

art.line: brush-pen over rough blue pencil; xerox grain; stark spotting; rain in frantic vertical hatching (Arc 1's aesthetic)

notes: Two coats, thirty years apart, drawn the same. Six strokes.
